notes.1: Heading XIII. begins the poem on printed page66. Both full pages have visible alternating insets, recorded explicitly. The source spelling is Faliscis.
notes.2: The source prints Moenia contigimus victa, Camille, tibi. with commas around Camille.
notes.4: The source prints indigenamque bovem with a final colon.
notes.6: The source word is clivis, retained as printed.
notes.7: The printed adjective is praenubilus, retained without an imported replacement.
notes.8: The spelling is Adspice, followed by a colon; a semicolon ends the verse.
notes.11: The source prints praesonuit sollemni tibia cantu; the doubled l in sollemni is retained, with a final comma.
notes.15: Neither verse15 nor verse16 has terminal punctuation; verse17 ends in a semicolon.
notes.18: The source contraction Invisast is retained. The verse ends with a colon.
notes.20: The source prints inceptam destituisse fugam with a final semicolon before the page break.
notes.21: The printed verb is incessitur. The running head uses XIIII for the following poem14; the source numbering is retained in forme work.
notes.23: The printed contraction deast is retained without silently expanding it.
notes.24: The source prints Praeverrunt and a colon after vias.
notes.27: The source spelling is Graio, retained as printed.
notes.31: The printed contraction Argivast and the colon after facies are retained.
notes.32: The source proper name is Halaesus; verses32–33 have no terminal punctuation.
notes.36: The final verse has a comma after mihi and an exclamation mark after suo. The following heading XIIII. begins the next poem.
